Treat each individual closed container and each open surface as a separate candidate while keeping the sweep spread across receptacle types so new, not-yet-inspected candidates are reached (open each newly reached container once; if it lacks the target, continue to a different uninspected candidate instead of exhausting or looping over one type). Leave an already-open empty or duplicate location immediately. Use the current and last two observations not to return to a just-confirmed-empty location, and stop revisiting a recurring small set within the step budget. Preserve 'do not repeatedly check inventory while carrying nothing' and the find-or-cover-all completion boundary. adjustments.reason: In the current batch `P3` never acquires its apple and ends at the step limit (`P3:50`), cycling among the same already-seen locations (`P3:1`, `P3:13`, `P3:34`) instead of reaching any uninspected receptacle, which is precisely the `G1` problem; the successful runs instead reach a not-yet-inspected surface and acquire the exact target (`P1:34`, `P1:35`, `P2:8`, `P2:9`). Historical `M6` and `M10` record that the family-sweep/anti-cycling wording did not reliably prevent cycling, and even successful `P1` wastes steps re-entering open empty cabinets (`P1:24`, `P1:28`), so the locally usable trigger (leave an already-open empty location; do not return to a just-confirmed location) is the part worth strengthening. The Original's instruction to keep opening one container after another 'rather than considering a receptacle family finished after one or two members' is not supported: `P1` opened every cabinet and reached the countertop surface, yet its exact plate came from a different, previously uninspected surface, so per-type depth did not produce success and conflicts with the Parent's spread-across-types sweep (`P1:14`-`P1:33`). Aligning the sweep with the Parent while adding the local trigger keeps the direction; the coverage boundaries (no inventory checks while carrying nothing; stop when found or all plausible candidates inspected once) are retained. Transfer of the recurring-small-set trigger to fully-unknown rooms remains an unverified hypothesis.
